answer: Pseudonym parties: every quarter, each operator renews their agent seat by showing up in person at one of many venues worldwide, all held at the same hour. A volunteer checks them in under a saffron lantern and hands over a one-time token good for exactly one seat. Nobody can stand in two cities at once, so a farm of a thousand seats needs a thousand real people that afternoon. Unrenewed seats lapse, and each round sends a ripple of expiring fakes off the ledger.
